organism.common_frame: Early Devonian Rhynie Chert lycopsid (actinostele and microphylls)
organism.clade_note: Asteroxylon is a stem lycopsid, not an angiosperm. The campaign path label is retained; the biology used here is Kidston & Lang 1920 and Hetherington et al. 2021.

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Asteroxylon mackiei (5.2 µm, detail scale)
phenomenon_scale.calibration_note: 5.2 µm is the assigned detail-tier critical wavelength of this slot. It is not a published histological measurement of an Asteroxylon pigment period.

versus_scale_predecessor.name: Asteroxylon mackiei enation-spacing mode
versus_scale_predecessor.change: The 283 µm mode sets one wavelength across a microphyll primordium. The 5.2 µm mode is 54.5 times shorter, so about 30 critical wavelengths fit in a 156 µm tracheid-file window and the diffusion coefficients drop by the square of that ratio. Parameters are not copied from the sibling.

versus_grade_predecessor.name: Cooksonia pertoni
versus_grade_predecessor.change: Cooksonia is leafless and has no actinostele. There is no protoxylem-pole harmonic and no microphyll trace for a 5.2 µm wall-pattern mode to phase-lock to.

versus_grade_successor.name: Baragwanathia-grade microphyllous lycopsid
versus_grade_successor.change: Fully vascularized microphylls lengthen the organ-scale spacing. The subcellular 5.2 µm mode can persist as tracheid-wall annular or helical spacing while the organ wavelength grows. This slot does not simulate that successor.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg 1979: du/dt = a - u + u^2 v + D_u laplacian(u); dv/dt = b - u^2 v + D_v laplacian(v)
equations.jacobian: f_u = -1 + 2 u v; f_v = u^2; g_u = -2 u v; g_v = -u^2, evaluated at steady state
equations.homogeneous_stability: tr J = f_u + g_v < 0 and det J = f_u g_v - f_v g_u > 0
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.turing_inequality: (D_v f_u + D_u g_v)^2 > 4 D_u D_v det J, which requires D_v/D_u > 1/f_u

boundary_conditions.domain: periodic rectangle, 156.0 µm by 117.0 µm (30 by 22.5 critical wavelengths)
boundary_conditions.physical_meaning: one tracheid-file detail window, not a whole shoot
boundary_conditions.numerical: Fourier pseudospectral diffusion, explicit reaction, periodic

parameters.why_not_the_sibling: Sibling wavelength 283.4 µm uses a primordium-scale domain. Here D_u is fixed by k_c = 2 pi / 5.2 µm and delta = 160, which is an intracellular ratio, not a tissue-scale morphogen ratio.

empirical_claims.claim: Asteroxylon mackiei has a stellate xylem (actinostele) with leaf traces into microphylls.
The Rhynie Chert is Pragian, Early Devonian, about 407 Ma.
The plant is a branching aerial axis with microphylls and rooting axes that are not true roots.
Roots originated stepwise; Asteroxylon rooting axes are not homologous with euphyllophyte roots.
A two-species reaction-diffusion system selects a finite critical wavenumber k_c when the inhibitor diffuses sufficiently faster than the activator.
